title: What to Do After a Car Accident in Philadelphia
metaDescription: First steps after a Philadelphia crash: 911, photos, medical care, and 2-yr PA SOL. Not legal advice.
excerpt: Educational Philadelphia, PA guide — 2-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on I-95 or surface streets in Philadelphia can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 when anyone reports pain, airbags deploy, fluids leak, or traffic is blocked. Philadelphia County dispatch will route Philadelphia police or state patrol depending on location.
list: Stay inside the vehicle with seatbelts on if traffic passes closely at highway speed
Do not admit fault — describe facts only
Request a crash report number before officers leave

sections.heading: Philadelphia documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. Philadelphia insurers expect timestamped photos.
Collect names and phone numbers from witnesses — independent accounts matter on I-95, I-76, I-676 and in Philadelphia County.
Exchange insurance policy numbers and registration; note employer if the other driver was working.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: Philadelphia has Penn Presbyterian and Jefferson Health among its major facilities. Level I trauma care is available at Penn Presbyterian Medical Center.
Whiplash, concussion, and internal injuries may appear hours later. A same-day urgent care or ER visit creates a medical record insurers cannot easily dismiss.

sections.heading: Pennsylvania reporting rules
paragraphs: Pennsylvania requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 15/30/5.
Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through local police. If police do not respond, check https://www.penndot.pa.gov/ for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
Pennsylvania no-fault rules may limit lawsuits unless injuries exceed thresholds — verify with counsel.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in Philadelphia
paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near I-95 Girard Avenue is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
Save repair estimates, rental receipts, and mileage to medical appointments.

sections.heading: When to explore attorney matching
paragraphs: Consider a free consultation if you were hospitalized, fault is disputed, a commercial vehicle was involved, or the adjuster offers a quick settlement before treatment finishes.
WreckMatch LLC connects Philadelphia residents with licensed Pennsylvania attorneys — we are a referral service, not a law firm.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my Philadelphia case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Pennsylvania?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 2-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
